persona: Food chemist running a Folin-Ciocalteu total phenolic content (TPC) assay on eight plant/spice extracts, using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer whose software exports a raw report, into which the researcher then typed their own formula columns.
source_style: lab instrument software export (UVProbe) with researcher-added Excel formula columns layered on top

columns.name: Abs 1
columns.notes: Raw absorbance reading 1 at 765nm; one cell (Thyme, row 25) holds the text 'n.d.' instead of a number

columns.name: Mean Abs
columns.notes: Stored as the Excel formula '=AVERAGE(B:D)' for that row, NOT a static value; file has no cached result because it was generated programmatically rather than saved by Excel. Excel's AVERAGE ignores the 'n.d.' text cell for Thyme, averaging only the 2 numeric reads.

columns.name: Dilution Factor
columns.notes: 1 for undiluted samples, 5 for the three samples diluted 1:5 before reading

columns.name: TPC (mg GAE/g)
columns.notes: Stored as the Excel formula '=((MeanAbs-0.0123)/0.0089)*DilutionFactor*0.025' referencing the Mean Abs and Dilution Factor cells of the same row; also has no cached value in this file. True values given in clean_table.

intended_analysis: Compare TPC (mg GAE/g) across the 8 extracts (one-way ANOVA + Tukey post-hoc, or simple ranking) to identify which spice/plant extracts have the highest total phenolic content; the calibration block is a reference curve, not part of the comparison dataset.
mess_applied: Two stacked tables in one sheet: a 6-row calibration-standards block (rows 8-14) sits above the real sample data table (header at row 17) with no blank-column/sheet separation, only a blank row and an italic label row between them
5 rows of free-text instrument-header junk (rows 1-5) before any tabular data, including a merged title cell A1:G1
Default sheet name 'Sheet1' rather than a descriptive name

The 'Mean Abs' and 'TPC (mg GAE/g)' columns are Excel formulas with NO cached value (file built by a script, not saved by Excel), so a reader that doesn't evaluate formulas gets either the literal formula string or nothing at all for every sample's computed columns

One raw replicate (Thyme Extract, Abs 1) holds the text 'n.d.' instead of a number, inside an otherwise numeric column; Excel's AVERAGE silently drops it, so the true Mean Abs for that row is the average of only 2 of the 3 cells, not 3
3 free-text footer rows after the data (dilution note, calibration equation, and a legend for 'n.d.') that a naive reader might try to parse as more data rows

Sample naming inconsistent with the footer note: samples are called 'Cinnamon Extract' etc. in the table but referred to as 'Samples 6-8' in the footer, requiring positional cross-reference to know which rows were diluted
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A tool that just grabs 'the first table on the sheet' will scoop up the 6-row calibration standards as if they were sample data (or concatenate them with the real samples). A tool that reads cell values without formula evaluation will get None/blank or the raw formula text for every Mean Abs and TPC value instead of a number, and a tool that averages Abs1:Abs3 naively (treating 'n.d.' as 0 or as NaN-that-poisons-the-mean) will get the wrong Mean Abs for Thyme Extract instead of the 2-value average Excel actually computes.
